subject: Dedicated capacity configuration follow-up — GPU choice & TPS assumptions
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@crestview.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity configuration follow-up — GPU choice & TPS assumptions

Hi Jordan / team,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for walking through the Crestview inference workload. Per our discovery, I wanted to capture a few clarifying questions so we can size a Dedicated capacity recommendation (and surface Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private implications). Short version: two config options are likely to be sensible depending on TPS and latency SLOs — I list the items we need to finalize below.

Quick recap of what we heard on the call: 
- Model family: internal LLM (GPT-like) ~1.5B parameters (custom fine-tune).
- Primary use: real-time product recommendations + short answer assistant.
- Expected steady-state TPS: 120 concurrent requests per minute (bursty peaks up to ~600/min).
- Typical prompt length: 40–120 tokens; average generation length: 60 tokens.
- Latency target: p95 < 220ms end-to-end.

Clarifying items for sizing (can reply inline):
1) Token mix: do you have a token distribution (prompt vs gen length; any long-tail or batch jobs)? This matters for KV cache sizing and memory.
2) Peak concurrency: you gave burst rate in RPM; what is the peak concurrent in-flight requests you expect during a spike?
3) Cold-start tolerance: are occasional 500–800ms cold starts acceptable, or do you need <300ms always?
4) Security: will this run in our Dedicated shared tenancy or will you require Private (VPC/on-prem) for data residency?
5) Throughput targets: do you measure throughput as requests/sec or tokens/sec (helps pick GPU).

Initial suggestions (to speed up):
- If you need strict p95 <250ms and heavy burst handling, H100-class instances (or equivalent) give best headroom.
- For cost-sensitive steady TPS with moderate latency targets, A10G/A30-class setups are often more efficient.

Attachments: please share a simple token mix CSV if you have one (prompt/gen disaggregation) — I can turn that into quick ETA estimates.

Next steps: if you can reply with token mix + peak concurrent estimate I’ll return two concrete SKU+TPS+cost options and a suggested PoC plan (1-week smoke + 2-week load/quality run).

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity configuration follow-up — GPU choice & TPS assumptions

Thanks Dylan — good notes. See answers below and I attached a token mix CSV (crestview_token_mix_q1.csv).

Answers:
- Token mix (attached): median prompt 55 tokens, median gen 60 tokens, 95th percentile total tokens ~240. About 8% of calls are longer (500+ tokens) for batch summarization jobs.
- Peak concurrent: during promotion spikes we saw ~220 concurrent in-flight requests for a 3–5 minute window; sustained steady-state concurrent is ~30–40.
- Cold-start: we prefer p95 < 300ms for interactive UI. Occasional 600–800ms for background jobs is ok.
- Security: crestview requires a VPC option for production (data residency + private endpoints). We want to understand the Dedicated + VPC setup (is that your Private offering or an add-on to Dedicated?).
- Throughput metric: we think in RPS for UI flows and tokens/sec for background summarization.

Procurement note: we’ll need a rough estimate for committed monthly cost (order of magnitude) to model with finance — T-shirt estimates are fine at this stage.

Happy to hop on 30 mins tomorrow afternoon to go over config choices.

Best,
Jordan

Jordan — perfect, thanks for the CSV and the answers. I ran a quick back-of-envelope using your token mix and the peak concurrent number; below are two candidate Dedicated configurations and what they buy you. These assume our Dedicated pool with VPC peering (we can on-board via Private deployment if you need fully private control plane — I flag differences below).

Option A — Cost-efficient steady (A10G/A30 class)
- Target: steady 30–40 concurrent, handle bursts to ~220 with autoscale/queueing
- Expected p95 latency for median requests: ~180–300ms depending on exact prompt; p95 for worst-case long tails (500+ tokens) may approach 800–1,000ms without special batching
- GPUs: 4x A10G (or A30) equivalent in a pooled Dedicated cluster
- Concurrency model: 40 reserved concurrency + burst pool for autoscale; continuous KV cache enabled to reduce repeated prefix work
- Good if: cost matters, most calls are median-sized and UI latency target is ~250–300ms

Option B — Performance-focused (H100 class)
- Target: sustain 220 concurrent bursts with headroom for peaks and maintain p95 < 300ms for most interactive flows
- GPUs: 2–3x H100 (multi-card nodes) with aggressive batching and higher token throughput
- Concurrency model: higher per-GPU concurrency, larger KV cache allocation for long-tail jobs, specialized kernel selection for lower latency
- Good if: strict p95 <300ms requirement, a larger fraction of long generations, and you want fewer nodes to manage

Notes on Private vs Dedicated:
- Dedicated with VPC peering: private endpoints for API traffic, Redwood-managed control plane; faster to provision and lowers ops on your side.
- Private (customer-managed control plane / on-prem): required when you need the control plane in your VPC or full air-gapped installs, higher setup lead time and enterprise contract.

Suggested PoC: 1-week smoke on a small Dedicated pool (2x A10G) to validate token mix and latency, then a 2-week scaled load test on the chosen SKU (H100 or A30) before committing. I’ve linked a short PoC brief: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/crestview-poc-deck (deck includes success criteria and benchmark plan).

Estimated monthly T-shirt pricing (very rough):
- Option A (4x A10G pool): ~$23–30k/month committed
- Option B (3x H100 nodes): ~$55–75k/month committed

If that looks reasonable I’ll:
1) Draft a mutual action plan + timeline
2) Pull in our Private deployment lead if you want control-plane in VPC
3) Share a short benchmark runbook and schedule the PoC.

Can we do 30 minutes today 3:00–3:30pm PT for a quick alignment?

Thanks,
Dylan
